title: Shopify → Sheets → AI → Alerts
summary: Every new Shopify order is logged to Google Sheets, classified by AI for risk, priority and customer type, and flagged in Slack or by email when it needs a person.
result: Orders flagged as high risk, rush or VIP are sent to the team for review before fulfillment. A second check, not a replacement for Shopify's own fraud analysis.

metric.label: of manual order review per week, estimated for 40 orders a day at about 1 minute each, 7 days a week (40 × 1 min × 7 ≈ 4.7 h)

note: Demo built with simulated Shopify test orders sent to an n8n webhook. Tested in n8n end to end with the Claude API call mocked; Sheets, Slack and Gmail need your own credentials.

flow.label: New order sent to a webhook

upworkBlurb: n8n automation for a Shopify store: every new order hits a webhook, is logged to Google Sheets and classified by AI (Claude API) for fraud risk, shipping priority and customer type, with a one-line reason. Orders flagged as high risk, rush or VIP go to the team on Slack and email for review before fulfillment, as a second check next to Shopify's own fraud analysis. Designed to save about 5 hours a week (estimate based on 40 orders a day at about 1 minute each). Importable n8n workflow, test orders and setup guide included.

es.title: Shopify → Hoja → IA → Alertas
es.summary: Cada pedido nuevo de Shopify se registra en Google Sheets, la IA lo clasifica por riesgo, prioridad y tipo de cliente, y se avisa por Slack o correo cuando necesita a una persona.
es.result: Los pedidos marcados como riesgo alto, urgentes o VIP se envían al equipo para revisión antes del envío. Una segunda revisión, que no reemplaza el análisis de fraude de Shopify.
es.metricLabel: de revisión manual de pedidos por semana, estimadas para 40 pedidos al día a cerca de 1 minuto cada uno, 7 días a la semana (40 × 1 min × 7 ≈ 4,7 h)
es.note: Demo hecha con pedidos de prueba simulados de Shopify enviados a un webhook de n8n. Probado en n8n de punta a punta con la llamada a la API de Claude simulada; Sheets, Slack y Gmail necesitan tus propias credenciales.
